requirement:
`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider.
A criterion can compute its answer directly using tracked inputs; deterministic
execution needs no configured agent.
rationale:
The requirement has two obligations. `Criterion::execute` can compute an answer with no configured model provider. A criterion can compute its answer directly from tracked inputs, with no agent needed. The reviewed tests cover both.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[deterministic_validation_uses_required_storage_without_an_agent]`:
  - It builds `Validator::new(graph)` with no agent.
  - It runs `verify(Review(Node(1)))`, which succeeds.
  - It asserts the computed output: the result is false and the rationale equals "ordinary computation", the value read from the graph node.
  - After `store_evidence`, it asserts the saved evidence has a `Dependency::Node(Node(1), fingerprint)` whose fingerprint value is "ordinary computation". That shows the answer was computed from a tracked input.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agents_initialize_only_when_asked_and_report_setup_errors]`:
  - It configures an agent whose credential is missing, so any model call would fail.
  - A deterministic `refresh_evidence(Question(false))` still succeeds, with the expected output and one tracked dependency.
  - The agent provider is still uninitialized (`provider.get().is_none()`), and only the explicit agent-backed ask returns an `Agent` error. This shows deterministic execution does not touch the model provider even when one is configured but unusable.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[criteria_keep_typed_answers_and_persist_only_when_requested]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/validation.rs#fn[caller_reuses_negative_answers_and_compares_revisions_explicitly]`: both run `verify` on criteria with a plain `Validator` and no agent, and both assert the computed outputs, dependencies and execution counts. They add breadth, including the no-input case with empty dependencies.

I found no gap. The only distinction the text draws is between deterministic execution with no agent and execution with an unusable agent configured, and both are tested with assertions. No FIXME acknowledgments apply.
